$comment: DRAFT — not a shipped contract. Authority: docs/01-CONTRACT.md §8, docs/03-V0-SCOPE.md §1 item 13. Six variants, borrowed in shape from Anydoc (parity checklist A5).
title: Engine error taxonomy (DRAFT)
description: The point is that a caller can ROUTE on the kind. 'This document is encrypted' and 'this document is complex' must never arrive as the same signal — the defect LiteParse's single exit code has, where password-protected, invalid-header, corrupt-header and missing-file all exit 1 identically to 'complex'. Failing closed with an indistinguishable signal is still a defect.

oneOf.title: Unsupported
oneOf.description: A format, version, or feature this profile does not claim to handle. Distinct from malformed: the document may be perfectly valid and the gap is ours. Maps to a capability-limited result, never a negative conclusion — absence of extractable content is never evidence of absence in the source.

oneOf.title: Malformed
oneOf.description: The input violates its own format specification.

oneOf.title: Encrypted
oneOf.description: Its own variant rather than a malformed sub-case, because it is the canonical example of an outcome a caller routes differently: a human can supply a password, and no amount of retrying fixes it otherwise.

oneOf.title: ResourceLimit
oneOf.description: A declared bound was hit. Partial work is discarded rather than emitted: a truncated representation that looks complete is worse than no representation.

oneOf.title: MissingPart
oneOf.description: A structure the format requires was absent.

oneOf.title: Io
oneOf.description: An I/O failure reading the source. Carries a string rather than a system error so the value stays comparable and serializable — an error that cannot appear in a diagnostic artifact is not much use to a fail-closed design.
